strings.うずくまった丸い形は、転がりにくい底の広いダルマと同じで、台に置けば重さの真ん中: A crouching round shape is the same as a Daruma with a wide base that does not roll easily: if you set it on a stand, the middle of its weight (the center of gravity) is low, and it comes back when pushed. If the idea is that it floats on water, it is like a toy that floats in the bath: a light hollow shell floats by as much as the water it pushes aside.

strings.かざぐるまが回るのは、ひねった羽が風を横へそらし、そのお返しに羽が横へ押されるか: A pinwheel turns because the twisted blades push the wind to the side, and in return the blades are pushed to the side. It is like using the blades of an electric fan the other way around. The idea of folding the blades into little cups is like the cups of an anemometer or the buckets of a water wheel: the open side is pushed harder, so it turns.

strings.ここでは、おもちゃを選ぶと、すぐに紙の型紙を作れます。紙と糸で作って、動くかたし: Here, when you pick a toy, you can make its paper template right away. Make it with paper and string, and check whether it moves. The template is not the right answer. It is only a trial idea that the AI thought up (“maybe it is like this?”). The paper answers first. A record of a time it did not move also counts as {0} of the paper’s answers. Please write down what tweaks you made. This gives hints for making the next template better. After you write your own thoughts, you can get an answer from the AI (Claude) too. Even if it moves with paper, that does not mean we know how it was made long ago. It is not a copy of the old toy. It is a plan for making a trial.
strings.ここで言うおもちゃは、手で動かしてたしかめられる形（トイ＝モデル）のことです。買: By “toy” we mean a shape you can move with your hands to find out how it works (a toy = a model). It is not a finished product that someone buys for you, and it is not a copy that looks just like the real thing.

strings.これも何の作り物かはわからないので、置き方の仕組みでたとえます。台なしで置かれた: We do not know what this one is made to be either, so the comparison is about how it sits. A long thin thing placed with no stand stays still without rolling. It is the same as an eraser on a desk or a stone with a flat-cut bottom: the wider the bottom face, the steadier it is. As for the idea of floating it on water, it is like a boat floating in the bath.
strings.しなり: 柄に貼る長さが短いと、振った時に付け根の紙が曲がる。長く貼ると棒ごと動: Flex: If the part glued to the handle is short, the paper at the base bends when you wave it. If you glue a longer part, the whole stick moves.
strings.しなり: 竹串を貼った長さが短いと、振った時に紙が先にしなる。長く貼ると棒ごと動: Flex: If the part where the bamboo skewer is glued is short, the paper bends first when you wave it. If you glue a longer part, the whole stick moves.
strings.しなり: 竹串を貼った長さが短いと、振った時に紙の付け根が先に曲がる: Flex: If the part where the bamboo skewer is glued is short, the base of the paper bends first when you wave it.

strings.しなり: 細い棒に広い紙を付けて振ると、空気に押されて紙がしなる。貼る長さを長く: Bending: If you wave wide paper on a thin stick, the air pushes on the paper and it bends. If you glue on a longer length of stick, it bends less.
strings.しなり: 細い棒の先に紙を付けて振ると、紙は空気に押されてしなる。貼る長さを長く: Bending: if you wave paper on the tip of a thin stick, the air pushes the paper and it bends. The longer the glued length, the harder it is to bend.
strings.しなり: 細い棒や薄い紙は、根元を固定して先を振ると曲がる。貼る長さが短いほど紙: Bending: A thin stick or thin paper bends if you hold the base and swing the end. The shorter the glued length, the sooner the paper bends.

strings.すき間と摩擦: 切れ目が狭いと紙どうしがこすれて止まり、広いとぐらつく: Gaps and friction: If the slit is narrow, the paper rubs and gets stuck. If it is wide, it wobbles.
strings.すき間と摩擦: 狭いと紙どうしがこすれて止まり、広いと抜け落ちる。鉛筆とキャップ: Gap and friction: if the gap is narrow, paper rubs on paper and it stops; if it is wide, it falls out. Think of a pencil and its cap.

strings.ずんぐりした鳥の形は、底が広くて重さの真ん中（重心）が低いので、置物として倒れに: A chubby bird shape has a wide bottom and a low middle of weight (center of gravity), so it is a shape that does not tip over easily as an ornament. If we read it as papier-mâché, it is a light shell made of layers of glued paper, and it keeps its shape even if the inside is empty. It is made the same way as an eggshell or a piñata.

strings.てこ: 支点から遠い所ほど大きく動く。腰が支点なら、頭と杵の先が一番大きく振れる: Lever: the farther from the pivot, the more it moves. If the waist is the pivot, the head and the tip of the pestle swing the most.
strings.てこ: 支点（軸）から押す所が近いほど、動かす側は大きく動く。力は小さくてよいが: Lever: The closer the spot you push is to the pivot (axis), the more the moving side moves. The force can be small, but the distance moved is large.
strings.てこ: 袖が軸の近くで回るなら、糸を少し引くだけで袖の先は大きく上がる: Lever: if the sleeve turns near the pivot, pulling the string only a little raises the tip of the sleeve a lot.
strings.てこ: 軸の近くを少し動かすと、軸から遠い所は大きく動く。力は小さく、動きは大き: Lever: If you move a little near the axle, the part far from the axle moves a lot. The force is small, and the movement is big.
strings.てこ: 軸（支点）から遠い所ほど、同じ動きでも大きく振れる。はさみの刃の先と持ち: Lever: the farther a spot is from the pivot, the more it swings for the same push. Think of the tips of scissor blades and the handles.
strings.てこ: 軸（支点）の近くを少し動かすと、軸から遠い袖の先は大きく振れる: Lever: move a little near the pivot (fulcrum), and the tips of the sleeves, far from the pivot, swing a lot
strings.てこ: 軸（支点）の近くを少し動かすと、遠い所は大きく動く。くちばしの先が大きく: Lever: If you move a spot near the axis (pivot) a little, a spot far away moves a lot. This is why the tip of the beak swings a lot.
strings.てこ: 軸（支点）の近くを少し引くと、軸から遠い所は大きく動く: Lever: pull a little near the pivot (fulcrum), and the parts far from the pivot move a lot
strings.てこ: 軸（支点）の近くを少し引くと、軸から遠い頭の先は大きく動く: Lever: pull a little near the pivot (fulcrum), and the tip of the head, far from the pivot, moves a lot
strings.てこと柄: 長い柄は小さな力で持ち上げられるが、先が重いと手元で支える力が要る: Lever and handle: a long handle can be lifted with little force, but if the end is heavy you need force at your hand to hold it

In a workshop, this loop of learning from experience (the experiential learning cycle) goes around just once, together with a facilitator. With utsushi, you can keep it going on your own afterward. The idea of pushing and pulling the stand with the long handle to ring the balls inside is like a rattle, or a toy car that makes a sound when it rolls.
strings.台に立てた人形が指で押しても戻るのは、台の上の写真立てや置き時計と同じで、重さの: A doll standing on a stand comes back when you push it with a finger, like a photo frame or a table clock on a stand: it does not fall over as long as the middle of its weight (the center of gravity) is above the surface of the stand. The idea of leaning it up with a support at the back is like the leg of a photo frame or a smartphone stand. The more you open the support, the steadier it is.
strings.台に立てた人形は、重さの真ん中（重心）が台の上にある間は倒れません。細長い人形は: A puppet standing on a base does not fall over as long as the middle of its weight (the center of gravity) is above the base. A tall, thin puppet tips easily, like a pencil stood on its end, and it becomes steadier if you make the base wider and the center of gravity lower. If the idea is that it leans against something, it is the same idea as the support at the back of a photo frame.
strings.台に立てた紙の亀は、重さの真ん中（重心）が台の上にある間は倒れません。机の端に消: A paper turtle standing on a base does not fall over as long as the middle of its weight (the center of gravity) is above the base. It is like the game of putting an eraser at the edge of a desk and sliding it out a little at a time: it falls when the center of gravity moves outside the base. If the idea is that it floats on water, it is like a rubber duck toy that floats in the bath.

strings.小さな兜の形は、低くて幅が広いので、置物として倒れにくい形です。帽子を机に伏せて: A small helmet is low and wide, so it is a shape that does not tip over easily as an ornament. strings.小さな社殿の置物が倒れずに立つのは、広い台に載せたドールハウスや積み木の家と同じ: A small shrine ornament stands without falling over, like a dollhouse or a block house set on a wide stand: as long as the middle of its weight (the center of gravity) is above the surface of the stand, it comes back. It is like a plastic bottle with a weight in the bottom, or a roly-poly piggy bank. When the middle of the weight (center of gravity) is low and the bottom is round, the weight pulls it back the way it was when you tilt it. The idea of standing on a flat bottom is like an ornament on a table.

It is like a plush toy sitting heavily, or a low flowerpot: the lower the middle of the weight (center of gravity) and the wider the supporting surface, the more it comes back when pushed.
strings.座って桃を抱いた猿の形は、底が広くて低いので、置物として倒れにくい形です。座った: A monkey sitting and holding a peach has a wide, low bottom, so it is a shape that does not tip over easily as an ornament. If we read it as a clay doll, it stands by its weight, but paper is made to stand with a wide bottom.

strings.息で動かす: 水に浮いた軽い物は、息の小さな力でも動く。帆の向きで曲がり方が変わ: Moving it with your breath: a light thing floating on water moves even with the small force of your breath. How it turns changes with the direction of the sail.
strings.息で動かす: 風の当たる面が大きいほど、小さな息でも進む。帆かけ舟と同じ: Moving by breath: The bigger the surface the wind hits, the more it moves even with a small breath. It is the same as a sailboat.
strings.息で回った。羽を少し反らせたら止まりにくい: It spun when I blew on it. When I curved the blades a little, it was harder to stop.
strings.息で進む: 息が当たる面（ひれや背）があると、小さな風でも進む。帆の向きで曲がる: Moving by breath: If there is a surface for your breath to hit (the fins or the back), it moves even in a small wind. It turns depending on the direction of the sail.
strings.息の向き: 真上から吹くより、横から吹く方が進む。風の当たる面に力がかかる: Direction of your breath: Blowing from the side makes it move better than blowing from straight above. The force acts on the surface the wind hits.

strings.打つ面: 板の面が広いほど、羽根に当てやすい。重い板は振るのに力が要るが、羽根を: Hitting surface: the wider the face of the board, the easier it is to hit the shuttlecock. A heavy board takes more force to swing, but sends the shuttlecock flying farther

strings.折り目のばね: 紙は折ると、折り目が少し戻ろうとする。折った紙を机に置くと浮くの: Crease spring: when you fold paper, the crease tries to spring back a little. When you put folded paper on a desk and it lifts up, that is this force.

strings.振り子: 吊った物を揺らすと、戻る力で行ったり来たりする。糸が長いほどゆっくり: Pendulum: If you swing a hanging thing, it goes back and forth because of the force that pulls it back. The longer the string, the slower it swings.
strings.振り子: 戻る力があると行き過ぎて反対へ揺れ、だんだん小さくなって止まる（空気と: Pendulum: With a force that pulls it back, it swings past the middle to the other side, gets smaller and smaller, and stops (because of the air and the rubbing at the axis).
strings.振り子: 揺れは行ったり来たりしてだんだん小さくなる。軸のこすれが大きいとすぐ止: Pendulum: The swing goes back and forth and gets smaller and smaller. If there is a lot of rubbing at the axis, it stops quickly.
strings.振り子の速さ: 重心が軸から遠いほど、揺れはゆっくり。近いほど小刻みに揺れる: Pendulum speed: The farther the center of gravity is from the axis, the slower the swing. The closer it is, the more it swings in small quick motions.

strings.掲げる物: 旗や幟のように、棒の先に付けて高く見せる物は、風を受けると棒がしなる: Things held up: things like flags and banners, fixed to the end of a stick to look tall, make the stick bend when they catch the wind
strings.揺らして鳴る: 中に玉があれば、打たなくても揺らすだけで壁に当たって鳴る: Sound from rocking: If there are balls inside, they hit the wall and sound just by rocking it, without hitting it.
strings.揺れの続き: 軸でこすれる力が小さいほど、揺れが長く続く: How long it keeps swinging: The less the rubbing force at the axle, the longer the swinging lasts.
strings.揺れの速さ: 重りを軸から遠くすると、揺れはゆっくりになる（長い振り子ほどゆっく: Swinging speed: If you put the weight farther from the axis, the swing gets slower (a longer pendulum swings more slowly).
strings.摩擦: 先がとがっていると床とこすれる所が小さく、勢いが減りにくい: Friction: If the tip is pointed, the part that rubs the floor is small, and the energy does not drop as fast.
strings.摩擦: 差した矢が止まるのは紙どうしがこすれる力。きつすぎると抜けない: Friction: an arrow stays in place because of the rubbing force between the papers. If it is too tight, it will not come out
strings.摩擦: 床と芯の先がこすれると回りが弱まる。つるつるの床ほど長く回る: Friction: when the tip of the core rubs on the floor, the spinning gets weaker. The smoother the floor, the longer it spins
strings.摩擦: 矢が袋の中で止まるのは、紙どうしがこすれる力。きつすぎると抜けない: Friction: An arrow stays in the bag because of the force of paper rubbing on paper. If it is too tight, it will not come out.
strings.摩擦: 筒の中で紙どうしがこすれると、戻る力の一部がそこで使われて、途中で止まる: Friction: when paper rubs against paper inside the tube, part of the springing-back force is used up there, and it stops halfway.
strings.摩擦: 軸の穴がきつすぎると動きが鈍く、ゆるすぎるとぐらつく。竹串を通す穴の大き: Friction: if the hole for the pivot is too tight, it moves slowly. If it is too loose, it wobbles. It changes with the size of the hole the bamboo skewer goes through.
strings.支え: 後ろに足を開くと、底の面が三角に広がる（写真立て・イーゼルと同じ）: Support: If you open a leg at the back, the bottom surface spreads into a triangle (the same as a photo frame or an easel).
strings.支えの角度: 立てかける支えは、開く角度が大きいほど倒れにくいが、場所を取る: Angle of the support: The wider the support opens, the harder it is to knock over, but it takes up more room.
strings.支える面: {0} 本の足の先を結んだ四角。細長い四角は、短い辺の向きに倒れやす: Supporting area: The four-sided shape made by joining the tips of the {0} legs. A long, thin four-sided shape tips easily in the direction of its short side.
strings.支える面: 丸い底でも、台に触れる所が広ければ倒れにくい: Supporting area: Even with a round bottom, it is harder to tip if the part touching the base is wide.
strings.支える面: 台が広いほど、倒れるまでに大きく傾けられる。甲羅の低い亀は重心も低い: Supporting area: The wider the base, the more you can tilt it before it falls. A turtle with a low shell also has a low center of gravity.
strings.支える面: 台と、立てかけた時の支えの足元が作る三角形。広いほど倒れにくい: Supporting area: The triangle made by the base and the foot of the support when it leans. The wider it is, the harder it is to tip.
strings.支える面: 底が丸いと台に触れる所が狭い。紙の台を付けると面が広がる: Supporting surface: if the bottom is round, only a small spot touches the stand. Adding a paper base makes the surface wider
strings.支える面: 底の広さ。しぼった口が上にあると、上は軽くて細い形になる: Supporting surface: how wide the bottom is. With the tightened mouth at the top, the upper part becomes light and narrow
strings.支える面: 底の広さ。首が細くても、底が広ければ安定する: Supporting area: The width of the bottom. Even with a thin neck, it is steady if the bottom is wide.
strings.支える面: 脚の底の広さ。脚を広げるほど倒れにくい（三脚やグラスの足と同じ）: Supporting area: The width of the bottom of the foot. The wider you spread the foot, the harder it is to tip (the same as a tripod or the foot of a glass).
strings.支える面: 足や台が作る面が広いほど倒れにくい。{0} 本足の亀は面が広い: Supporting area: The wider the area made by the legs or the base, the harder it is to tip. A turtle with {0} legs has a wide area.
strings.支える面: 足や台の縁を結んだ形。この面の外に重心が出ると倒れる: Supporting area: The shape you get by joining the edges of the feet or the base. If the center of gravity goes outside this area, it falls over.
strings.支える面: 足や台の縁を結んだ形。胴が長い犬は前後の足の間が広く、前後には倒れに: Supporting area: The shape you get by joining the edges of the feet or the base. A dog with a long body has a wide gap between its front and back legs, so it does not tip forward or backward easily.
strings.支える面: 鍋の底が台に触れる広さ。平らな底ほど安定する: Supporting surface: how wide the bottom of the pot touches the stand. A flatter bottom is more stable
strings.支えを {0}° くらい開き、机に立てる: Open the support about {0}° and stand it on a desk.

strings.足を開く: 両足の間を広げると支える面が広がる。揺れる電車で足を開いて立つのと同: Opening the feet: If you widen the space between the feet, the supporting surface gets wider. It is the same as standing with your feet apart on a shaking train.
strings.車の付いた台を糸で引く仮説は、引き車や、紐で引く木のおもちゃと同じです。車が台の: The idea of pulling a stand with wheels by a string works like a pull cart, or a wooden toy you pull with a cord. When the wheels turn in the holes of the stand, the stand rolls along without scraping the floor. The idea of putting it on a slope is like letting a toy car run down a slope: its weight pushes it in the downhill direction.
strings.車の大きさ: 車の半径が、軸から台の縁までより小さいと、台が床に触れてこすれる: Wheel size: if the wheel's radius is smaller than the distance from the axle to the edge of the stand, the stand touches the floor and rubs
strings.転がり: 丸い物は床とこすれる所が点か線だけなので、滑るより小さな力で動く: Rolling: a round thing touches the floor only at a point or a line, so it moves with less force than sliding
strings.転がり: 車が回ると、床とこすれる力がとても小さくなる。引きずるより軽く動くわけ: Rolling: when a wheel turns, the rubbing force against the floor gets very small. That is why it moves more easily than when it is dragged
strings.転がり: 車が軸の周りで回ると、床をこすらずに進める。引きずるより小さな力で動く: Rolling: When a wheel turns around its axle, it moves without rubbing the floor. It moves with less force than dragging.
strings.軸: 真ん中に軸を通して引くと、俵は軸の周りで回りながら進む（糸巻きと同じ）: Axle: if you put an axle through the middle and pull, the bale turns around the axle as it moves (the same as a spool)
strings.軸と前の壁の間（mm）: Gap between the axle and the front wall (mm)
strings.軸の摩擦: 軸が穴でこすれると回りにくい。穴を少し大きくするか、ビーズを挟む: Friction at the axle: if the axle rubs in the hole, it is hard to turn. Make the hole a little bigger, or put a bead between
strings.軸の摩擦: 軸が穴の中でこすれると回りにくい。穴を少し大きくするか、軸を滑らかに: Friction at the axle: if the axle rubs in the hole, it is hard to turn. Make the hole a little bigger, or make the axle smooth
strings.軽さ: 軽い置物は押されて動きやすいが、倒れても壊れにくい: Lightness: A light ornament is easy to push around, but it does not break easily even if it falls.

strings.重い胴: 外側が重い独楽は、回る勢いがたまって長く回る（はずみ車）: Heavy body: A top with a heavy outside stores spinning energy and spins longer (flywheel).
strings.重さで戻る: 上半身の方が重いと、糸を離した時に自分の重さで元へ戻る。戻る速さは: Returning by weight: if the upper body is heavier, it returns by its own weight when you let go of the string. How fast it returns depends on the weight and on how much the pivot rubs.
strings.重さで戻る: 軸の片側が重いと、離した時に重い方が下がって元の向きへ戻る: Returning by weight: if one side of the pivot is heavy, then when you let go, the heavy side goes down and it returns to its first position.
strings.重さの分け方: 重さが芯の周りに均等だと、回っても芯がぶれない。片寄ると首を振る: How the weight is divided: If the weight is even around the core, the core does not wobble when it spins. If the weight leans to one side, the top wobbles.
strings.重さの置き方: 円盤の外側が重いほど回る勢いがたまり、長く回る（はずみ車と同じ）: Where the weight sits: The heavier the outside of the disc, the more spinning energy it stores, and the longer it spins (the same as a flywheel).
strings.重ねて強くする: 薄い紙でも {0} 枚貼り合わせると曲がりにくい。厚みが曲がり: Stacking to make it strong: Even thin paper is harder to bend when you glue {0} sheet(s) together. The thickness decides how hard it is to bend.
strings.重ねる: 上に重い物を重ねると重心が上がり、倒れやすくなる。釜は風炉より小さいの: Stacking: If you stack a heavy thing on top, the center of gravity goes up, and it tips over more easily. The kettle is smaller than the brazier, so the effect is small.
strings.重ねる: 盃を台に載せるだけの時は、{0} つの重心が縦に並ぶ。ずれると落ちる: Stacking: When you just set the cup on the stand, the {0} centers of gravity line up vertically. If they shift, it falls.

strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。つる（取っ手）で吊ると、重心が真下に来る向きで止まる: Center of gravity: The middle of an object's weight. When you hang it by the handle, it stops in the position where the center of gravity is right below.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。上が広い形は重心が高く、少しの傾きで台の外へ出やすい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object's weight. A shape that is wide at the top has a high center of gravity, and a small tilt easily moves it outside the base.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。下がふくらんだ形は重心が低く、押しても戻りやすい: Center of gravity: the middle of an object's weight. A shape that bulges at the bottom has a low center of gravity and comes back easily even if pushed
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。低いほど、傾けても戻りやすい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object's weight. The lower it is, the easier it is for the object to come back after you tilt it.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。低いほど、押しても戻りやすい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object's weight. The lower it is, the easier it is for the object to come back when you push it.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。低くて、支える面の真ん中に近いほど倒れにくい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object's weight. The lower it is and the closer to the middle of the supporting area, the harder it is to tip.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。台の上にある間は、押しても元へ戻る: Center of gravity: The middle of an object's weight. As long as it is above the base, the object goes back to its first position even if you push it.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。底が広く下が重いほど低くなり、倒れにくい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object's weight. The wider the bottom and the heavier the lower part, the lower it is, and the harder it is to tip.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。柄が長いと重心が柄の側へ寄り、台からはみ出すと傾く: Center of gravity: the middle of an object's weight. With a long handle, the center of gravity moves toward the handle, and if it goes past the edge of the stand, the pot tips
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。背の高い人形ほど重心も高く、少しの傾きで台の外へ出る: Center of gravity: The middle of an object's weight. The taller the puppet, the higher the center of gravity, and a small tilt moves it outside the base.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。袋は底に中身がたまるので重心が低く、倒れにくい: Center of gravity: the middle of an object's weight. The contents of a bag collect at the bottom, so the center of gravity is low and it is hard to knock over
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。軸より下にあると、傾けた時に戻る向きの力が生まれる: Center of gravity: The middle of an object's weight. When it is below the axis, a force that pulls it back appears when you tilt it.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。軸より下に置くと、傾いた時に戻る向きの力が出る: Center of gravity: The middle of an object's weight. If you put it below the axis, a force that pulls it back appears when it tilts.
strings.重心: 物の重さの真ん中。首が高く上がった馬は重心が前寄りで、前へ倒れやすい: Center of gravity: The middle of an object's weight. A horse with its neck held high has its center of gravity toward the front, and it tips forward easily.
strings.重心: 重さの真ん中が低いほど、揺らしても戻りやすい。下に重りを入れた起き上がり: Center of gravity: the lower the middle of the weight, the more easily it comes back after rocking. This is the idea behind a tumbler toy (okiagari-koboshi) with a weight at the bottom.
strings.重心が低い: 重い所が底にあると、傾けても重心は少ししか上がらず、戻る力が働く: Low center of gravity: If the heavy part is at the bottom, the center of gravity goes up only a little when you tilt it, and a force that brings it back works.
strings.重心が軸より下: 吊るした物は、重い所が一番下に来る向きで止まる。傾けると戻ろう: Center of gravity below the pivot: a hanging thing settles with its heavy part at the very bottom. If you tilt it, it tries to come back and swings.
strings.重心と底: 細い首は軽いので重心は低い。底が広いと支える面も広く、戻る力が大きい: Center of gravity and bottom: A thin neck is light, so the center of gravity stays low. If the bottom is wide, the supporting surface is wide too, and the force that brings it back is big.
strings.重心と支える面: 下が広く重い形は重心が低い。傾けても重心が底の面の外へ出にくい: Center of gravity and supporting surface: A shape that is wide and heavy at the bottom has a low center of gravity. The center of gravity is less likely to move outside the bottom surface even when tilted.
strings.重心と支える面: 丸くて低い形は重心が低く、支える面も広いので戻りやすい: Center of gravity and supporting surface: A round, low shape has a low center of gravity and a wide supporting surface, so it comes back easily.
strings.重心と支える面: 人形が高く細いほど重心が高く、少しの傾きで倒れる。台を広くする: Center of gravity and supporting surface: The taller and thinner the doll, the higher the center of gravity, and the more easily it falls over with a small tilt. If you make the stand wider, it comes back more easily.
strings.重心と支える面: 低くて広い形は、傾けても重心が面の外へ出にくい: Center of gravity and supporting surface: A low, wide shape is less likely to have its center of gravity move outside the surface, even when tilted.
strings.重心と支える面: 傾けて重心が台の外へ出た時に倒れる。台が広いほど粘る: Center of gravity and supporting surface: it falls when you tilt it and the center of gravity goes outside the base. The wider the base, the longer it holds on
strings.重心と支える面: 台に立てる時は、台の広さと絵の高さで倒れやすさが決まる: Center of gravity and supporting surface: When you stand it on a stand, how easily it falls over depends on the width of the stand and the height of the picture.
strings.重心と支える面: 台に置く時は、底が広く低いほど倒れにくい: Center of gravity and supporting surface: When you set it on a stand, the wider and lower the base, the harder it is to knock over.
strings.重心と支える面: 台に置く時は、長い向きには倒れにくく、短い向きに倒れやすい: Center of gravity and supporting area: When you stand it on a base, it does not tip easily along the long direction, but it tips easily along the short direction.
strings.重心と支える面: 底が広く屋根が軽いと重心が低い。傾けても戻る: Center of gravity and supporting surface: If the bottom is wide and the roof is light, the center of gravity is low. It comes back even when tilted.
strings.重心と支える面: 底が広く背が低いほど、倒れにくい。ふたを重くすると重心が上がる: Center of gravity and supporting surface: The wider the base and the lower the height, the harder it is to knock over. If you make the lid heavy, the center of gravity goes up.
strings.重心と支える面: 底が広く背が低いほど、傾けても倒れにくい。屋根が重いと重心が上: Center of gravity and supporting surface: The wider the base and the lower the height, the harder it is to knock over, even when tilted. If the roof is heavy, the center of gravity goes up and it falls over more easily.
strings.重心と支える面: 底の箱が広く重いと重心が低い。上に伸びる幟は軽いので重心はあま: Center of gravity and supporting surface: If the box at the bottom is wide and heavy, the center of gravity is low. The banner reaching upward is light, so the center of gravity does not go up much.
strings.重心と支える面: 座った形は重心が低く、底の面が広い。傾けても重心が面の外へ出に: Center of gravity and supporting surface: A sitting shape has a low center of gravity and a wide bottom surface. The center of gravity is less likely to move outside the surface even when tilted.
strings.重心と支える面: 裾が広いと支える面が広く、傾けても重心が面の外へ出にくい: Center of gravity and supporting surface: If the hem is wide, the supporting surface is wide, and the center of gravity is less likely to move outside the surface even when tilted.
strings.重心と支える面: 裾が広いほど支える面が広く、傾けても戻りやすい。頭が重いと倒れ: Center of gravity and supporting surface: The wider the hem, the wider the supporting surface, and the more easily it comes back when tilted. If the head is heavy, it falls over more easily.
strings.重心と支える面: 足が細く体が高いと重心が高く、少しの傾きで倒れる。台を広げると: Center of gravity and supporting surface: If the legs are thin and the body is tall, the center of gravity is high, and it falls over with a small tilt. If you widen the stand, it comes back.
strings.重心と支える面: 重さの真ん中が底の面の真上にある間は、傾けても戻る。はみ出すと: Center of gravity and the face that holds it up: as long as the middle of the weight is right above the base, it comes back when you tilt it. If it goes past the edge, it falls.
strings.重心と支える面: 重心が底の面の上にある間は戻る。幅が広く低い形ほど、傾けられる: Center of gravity and supporting surface: While the center of gravity is above the base surface, it comes back. The wider and lower the shape, the bigger the angle you can tilt it.
strings.重心と支える面: 重心が底の面の上にある間は戻る。幅の広い体は傾けても粘る: Center of gravity and supporting surface: While the center of gravity is above the base surface, it comes back. A wide body hangs on even when tilted.
strings.重心と支える面: 重心が底の面の上にある間は戻る。座った形は重心が低く、面が広い: Center of gravity and supporting surface: While the center of gravity is above the base surface, it comes back. A sitting shape has a low center of gravity and a wide surface.
strings.重心と支える面: 重心が底の面の上にある間は戻る。細長い物ほど、傾けられる角度は: Center of gravity and supporting surface: it comes back as long as the center of gravity is above the bottom surface. The thinner and taller the object, the smaller the angle it can be tilted
strings.重心と支える面: 開く角度が広いほど、底の面が広がり、少し押しても戻る: Center of weight and supporting surface: The wider the opening angle, the wider the bottom surface, and it comes back even if you push it a little.
strings.重心と支点: 重心が支点より下にあると、傾けた時に戻る向きの力が働く。上にあると: Center of gravity and pivot: If the center of gravity is below the pivot, a force that pushes it back works when it tilts. If it is above, it falls over.
strings.重心と軸: あごの重い方が下がって元へ戻るので、糸を離すと口が元の形に戻る: Center of weight and axle: The heavier side of the jaw goes down and returns, so when you let go of the string, the mouth goes back to its original shape.
strings.重心と軸: 重心が軸より下にあると、傾けた時に戻る力が生まれ、振り子のように揺れ: Center of gravity and axis: When the center of gravity is below the axis, a force that pulls it back appears when you tilt it, and it swings like a pendulum.
strings.重心と軸: 頭の重さの真ん中が軸より下にあると、傾けても元に戻ろうとして揺れる（: Center of weight and axle: If the middle of the head's weight is below the axle, it tries to go back when tilted, and it swings (a pendulum).
strings.重心と軸: 顎の重さの真ん中が軸より前にあると、何もしなくても口が開く: Center of weight and axle: If the middle of the jaw's weight is in front of the axle, the mouth opens by itself.
strings.重心と軸: 鳥の重さの真ん中が軸より下にあると、傾けても元に戻ろうとして揺れる（: Center of weight and axle: If the middle of the bird's weight is below the axle, it tries to go back when tilted, and it swings (a pendulum).
strings.重心のずれ: 片側に長い物を付けると重さの真ん中がその側へ寄る。台をその向きに広: Shifted center of gravity: If you attach something long to one side, the middle of the weight moves toward that side. If you make the stand wider in that direction, it comes back more easily.

strings.面の大きさ: 大きいほど一度に押す空気が多い。そのぶん空気の押し返しも強く、紙が: Size of the face: The bigger it is, the more air it pushes at once. The air also pushes back harder, so the paper bends.
strings.面の張り: ぴんと張った面は高い音、ゆるい面は低くてこもった音。紙の面は張りが弱: How tight the face is: A tight face gives a high sound, and a loose face gives a low, muffled sound. A paper face is not very tight, so the sound is on the quiet side.
strings.面の震え: 太鼓の面を打つと面が震えて空気を揺らし、音になる。胴が空だと響く: Shaking of the face: When you hit the face of a drum, the face shakes and moves the air, and it becomes sound. It rings out when the body is hollow.

strings.頭が揺れて戻るのは、やじろべえや、ゆりかごと同じです。頭の下に重りを付けて、重さ: A head that swings and comes back is like a yajirobe (balancing toy) or a cradle. If you put a weight under the head so that the middle of its weight (the center of gravity) is below the axis, it comes back to its first position even if you tilt it. If the idea is that it swings in the wind, it is like a weather vane or a streamer.

strings.額に当て、糸を頭の後ろで結ぶ。力を入れすぎず、手でゆっくり動かす: Hold it against your forehead and tie the string at the back of your head. Do not use too much force. Move it slowly by hand.
strings.顔を棒の先に付けてかざすのは、紙のお面や応援のうちわと同じで、棒を貼った長さが短: Holding up a face on the end of a stick is like a paper mask or a cheering fan. If the part of the stick that is glued on is short, the paper bends first when you wave it. The idea that the tongue goes in and out of a slit in the mouth is like a drawer or a card slot: how easily it moves depends on how wide the gap is.
strings.風: 幟の布や紙は風を受けて揺れる（吹き流し・旗と同じ）: Wind: The cloth or paper of the banner catches the wind and sways (the same as a streamer or a flag).
strings.風で車が回るのは、かざぐるまや、川の水車と同じです。羽をひねっておくと、正面から: A wheel that spins in the wind is like a pinwheel or a river waterwheel. If you twist the blades, wind coming from the front is turned aside by the blades, and in return the blades are pushed and spin. If the idea is that a striker hits the drum, it is like the machine in which a waterwheel pounds a mortar.
strings.風と帆: 帆が少し上を向くと、風は下へ流れ、帆は上へ押される（手のひらを窓から出: Wind and sail: when the sail faces a little upward, the wind flows downward and the sail is pushed up (you can try it by putting your palm out of a window)
strings.風と帆: 帆が風に対して少し上を向くと、風が下へ流れて帆が持ち上がる: Wind and sail: when the sail faces a little upward to the wind, the wind flows downward and the sail is lifted
strings.風と帆: 風は帆に当たって下へ流れ、その分だけ帆を上へ押す: Wind and sail: the wind hits the sail and flows downward, and it pushes the sail up by that much
strings.風を受ける面: 四角い箱は平らな面が風を受け、風の向きへ回ろうとする: Surface that catches wind: A square box catches the wind on its flat side and tries to turn along the direction of the wind.
strings.風を受ける面: 平らな面に風が当たると、面が風下へ押される。吹流しの筒は風を通し: Surface that catches wind: when wind hits a flat surface, the surface is pushed downwind. A streamer tube lets the wind through as it flutters
strings.風上に向かって揚げ糸を少しずつ出す: Face into the wind and let out the kite string a little at a time

strings.魚の形を水に浮かべる仮説なら、笹舟や紙の船に似ていて、中が空の軽い殻は押しのけた: If the idea is that the fish shape floats on water, it is like a bamboo-leaf boat or a paper boat. A light, hollow shell floats because of the water it pushes aside, and if you blow on it, it moves like a sail. A long, flat shape does not roll sideways easily, just like a boat. Even if the idea is to stand it on a base, it is a shape that does not tip over along the long direction of its bottom.
strings.鳥の形の帆が風を受けて上がります。走って風を受けながら、ひもをぴんと張ると浮くの: A sail shaped like a bird catches the wind and goes up. When you run into the wind and pull the cord tight, it floats. This works the same way as a board pulled at an angle over water rising up. The tail and the curved rib keep the direction of the kite steady.
